q.q: Why do road signs mostly use pictures instead of words?
o: Pictures last longer in the rain than painted words
Pictures are cheaper to print than words on metal
They can be recognised instantly and get past language barriers
The law does not allow words on road signs
q.why: Signs must be understood at a glance by anyone, whatever language they speak.

q.q: A small café copies the Nike tick for its own sign. Why could it get into legal trouble?
o: Logos are protected by law as trademarks
Logos can only be used on road signs
q.why: Logos are so valuable they are protected by law as a trademark, so nobody else can use them.

q.q: Which of these is NOT one of the purposes of graphics listed in your notes?
q.why: Graphics entertain, promote, inform, advertise and educate (PIE AE).

q.q: How many colours should a good, easily printed logo use?
q.why: A good logo uses 3–5 colours, is simple and prints clearly.

q.q: What is a graphic?
o: Any piece of text written in a large, coloured font
Only a photograph taken with a digital or phone camera
Only an image drawn by hand on paper and then scanned
Any image, drawing, photo, logo or diagram shown on screen or printed
q.why: A graphic is any image, drawing, photo, logo or diagram shown on a screen or printed on paper.

q.q: A labelled diagram of the heart in your Biology book is mainly used to do what?
q.why: A labelled diagram teaches you, so its purpose is to educate.

q.q: A fire exit sign is an example of a graphic used to do what?
q.why: A fire exit sign gives information, so it informs.

q.q: Why do manufacturers spend millions of pounds on product packaging graphics?
o: How a product looks affects what you think of it
Graphics make the product last longer
The law says every package must have a picture
q.why: How a product looks affects what you think of it, so nearly all packaging carries a graphic.

q.q: What does CGI stand for?
q.why: CGI = Computer-Generated Imagery.

q.q: Which film was made entirely with CGI?
q.why: Shrek has no real actors on screen; the others mix CGI with actors.

q.q: Which part of an Avengers film is most likely to have been made with CGI?
o: The actors' faces in a quiet scene
The sound of the actors' voices
The real costumes the actors wear
q.why: Avengers films mix real actors with CGI such as the Hulk, Thanos and cities being destroyed.

q.q: In which film is CGI mixed with real actors, for example to create Gollum?
q.why: Lord of the Rings mixes CGI (Gollum, battle armies) with real actors; the others are fully CGI.

q.q: What is 'rendering' in CGI?
o: Printing the frames of a film onto paper
The computer working out what a frame looks like
Filming real actors in front of a green screen
Drawing a character by hand with a pencil
q.why: A single frame can take hours for powerful computers to work out, which is called rendering.

q.q: How many frames does a film show every second?
q.why: A film shows 24 frames every second.

q.q: Which of these is NOT a source of graphics?
q.why: A scanner only imports a graphic from paper; it is a device, not a source.

q.q: A designer wants to sketch a logo straight onto the computer as if drawing on paper. Which device should she use?
q.why: A graphics digitiser lets you draw straight onto the computer with a stylus.

q.q: You take a photo of the school rugby team on your phone. What is the source of the graphic?
q.why: A phone camera is a digital camera.

q.q: Which source would you need to scan in to use on the computer?
q.why: Printed images from magazines must be scanned to get them onto the computer.

q.q: What is clipart?
o: Images you draw yourself with a stylus on a graphics tablet
Pictures cut out of magazines and then scanned in
Ready-made drawings that come with software such as Word
Photos you take yourself on a phone during a school trip
q.why: Clipart is ready-made drawings that come with software such as Word or PowerPoint.

q.q: Why is a scanner not a source of graphics?
o: It can only scan in black and white, so it loses the colours
It only imports a graphic from paper; the source is the page you put in
It creates a brand new graphic itself without needing any paper
It is an output device that prints images, not an input device
q.why: A scanner is an input device that imports a graphic; the source is the drawing or magazine page.

q.q: What is the pen used with a graphics digitiser called?
q.why: You draw on a graphics digitiser with a special pen called a stylus.

q.q: You find a great photo on the internet for your school project. What should you do?
o: Change its colours so it counts as your own work
Say where you got it from, as most photos are copyrighted
Print it, then scan it back in to remove copyright
Use it freely, because everything online is free
q.why: Most photos are protected by copyright; for school work say where you got it from.

q.q: Which of these sources is described as older but still around?
q.why: Image collections sold on disc are older, but still around.

q.q: What does DPI stand for?
q.why: DPI = Dots Per Inch, a measure of print quality.

q.q: What happens when you scale up a low-resolution image?
q.why: The individual pixels become visible as jagged squares.

q.q: A 5 × 3 inch print is needed at 200 DPI. What pixel dimensions are needed?
q.why: Multiply each inch measurement by the DPI: 5 × 200 = 1000 and 3 × 200 = 600.

q.q: Which image will stay clearest when printed large?
o: A small image stretched to fit
q.why: More pixels means more detail to fill the larger print.

q.q: What is a pixel?
o: One dot of ink printed by a printer
A group of squares of different colours
A shape worked out using maths
One tiny square of a single colour
q.why: A pixel (picture element) is one tiny square and can be only one colour at a time.

q.q: What is meant by the resolution of an image?
o: How many layers the image has in Photoshop
How quickly the image downloads from a website
How many colours of ink a printer is able to use
How much detail it holds, linked to the number of pixels
q.why: Resolution is how much detail an image has, which depends on how many pixels it contains.

q.q: An image is 1920 × 1080. What are these numbers?
o: The number of colours and the number of layers
Its file size in kilobytes and megabytes
Its DPI for printing across and down
Its pixel dimensions: width and height in pixels
q.why: Pixel dimensions are the width and height of an image measured in pixels.

q.q: You need a 6 × 4 inch photo printed at 300 DPI. What pixel dimensions do you need?
Why doesn't stretching a small, low-resolution image make it sharp?
o: Stretching always changes the bitmap into a vector, which looks blurry
Stretching removes some of the colours from the image to save space
The computer has no extra detail to add, so it just makes each pixel bigger
The computer adds random extra pixels between the old ones, which blurs it
q.why: There is no extra detail, so each pixel is simply made bigger.

q.q: Why can an image that looks fine on screen look blocky when printed?
o: Screens need about 72–96 pixels per inch but prints need about 300 DPI
Printers can only print in black and white
Screens show fewer colours than printers
Printing always turns the image into a GIF
q.why: Screens look fine at 72–96 pixels per inch, but a sharp photo print needs around 300 DPI.

q.q: An image is 900 × 600 pixels. At 300 DPI, how big can it be printed?
q.why: Divide pixels by DPI: 900 ÷ 300 = 3 and 600 ÷ 300 = 2.

q.q: How many colours can be shown with 2 bits per pixel?
Using the key 00 = white, 01 = black, 10 = yellow, what is 'yellow, white, black'?
q.why: Yellow = 10, white = 00, black = 01.

q.q: What type of image is best for a detailed photograph?
q.why: Bitmaps store every pixel so they can hold photographic detail.

q.q: Why does a bitmap photo usually have a much bigger file size than a simple vector logo?
o: It is always saved at 300 DPI
It stores the maths for every shape
It stores information about every single pixel
It can only use 2 colours per pixel
q.why: A bitmap stores information about every pixel, so files are large.

q.q: What is colour depth?
o: The number of pixels across an image
The number of bits used for each pixel
The number of dots printed per inch
How dark the colours in an image are
q.why: The number of bits used for each pixel is called the colour depth.

q.q: How many colours can be shown with 3 bits per pixel?
How many colours can 8 bits per pixel show?
q.why: 8 bits gives 256 colours (00000000 to 11111111).

q.q: What is another name for a bitmap image?
q.why: A bitmap image is also called a raster image.

q.q: A bitmap is saved as a long list of binary codes. What else does the computer need to show the right colours?
o: A graphics digitiser to redraw the image
The DPI of the printer it will be printed on
A mathematical equation for every shape
A key (colour palette) saying what each code means
q.why: A bitmap is a list of numbers plus a key (the colour palette); without the key the numbers are meaningless.

q.q: Using the key 00 = white, 01 = black, 10 = yellow, 11 = red, what colours are '11 01 01 00'?
q.why: 11 = red, 01 = black, 01 = black, 00 = white.

q.q: Why does a vector image not go pixelated when you enlarge it?
o: It is redrawn from mathematical equations
It is always saved at 300 DPI
q.why: The shapes are recalculated from maths at the new size.

q.q: Which is the best choice for a company logo that will go on pens and on lorries?
q.why: Vectors scale to any size and stay sharp.

q.q: Why are vectors not used for photographs?
o: Photos must be printed, not shown on screen
Vector files are always very large
A photo would need far too many individual shapes
q.why: A photo has too much detail to describe with shapes.

q.q: Which file type is a vector format?
q.why: SVG stands for Scalable Vector Graphics; the others are bitmaps.

q.q: What is a vector graphic made from?
o: A grid of tiny coloured squares
Shapes, lines and curves worked out with maths
A list of binary codes for every pixel
q.why: A vector is calculated using mathematical equations that describe lines, curves and shapes.

q.q: Which package would you use to edit whole shapes in a vector image?
q.why: Vectors are edited as whole shapes in packages like Illustrator; bitmaps are edited pixel by pixel in Photoshop.

q.q: Which job is best suited to a bitmap?
o: A simple diagram of a circuit
A school logo for a badge
An icon for a website menu
A photo of a busy Enniskillen street
q.why: Photos are Bitmaps because they are Busy; logos, icons and diagrams suit vectors.

q.q: Which pair are both bitmap formats?
q.why: BMP, JPEG, PNG and GIF are bitmaps; SVG, AI and EPS are vectors.

q.q: How might a vector describe a red circle?
o: Pixel 1 red, pixel 2 red, pixel 3 red, and so on
A photo of a circle saved at 300 DPI
A circle, centre here, radius 50, filled red
q.why: A vector stores the maths for the shape, e.g. centre, radius and fill colour.

q.q: What happens to quality with lossy compression?
o: It is lost only until you reopen the file
q.why: Lossy compression permanently removes some detail.

q.q: Which format would keep a transparent background around a logo?
o: A JPEG saved at top quality
q.why: PNG supports transparency and is lossless.

q.q: Which format is lossy and best for photographs?
q.why: JPEG uses lossy compression and holds millions of colours.

q.q: Why should you save Photoshop work as a .psd file?
o: It keeps all your layers so you can edit later
It makes the file as small as possible
It turns the image into a vector
Every web browser can open it
q.why: PSD keeps layers and editing information.

q.q: What is compression?
o: Making an image bigger on screen without it going pixelated
Adding more colours to an image so it looks more detailed
Changing a bitmap image into a vector graphic so it scales
Making a file smaller so it takes less space and downloads faster
q.why: Compression makes a file smaller so it takes up less storage and downloads faster.

q.q: How does lossless compression make a file smaller?
o: It finds patterns, e.g. storing '5 × white' instead of white five times
It deletes the layers and keeps only the top one in the image
It removes tiny changes in colour that your eye is unlikely to notice
It reduces the image to only 256 colours, like a GIF does
q.why: Lossless finds patterns; nothing is thrown away.

q.q: Why does a photo saved as a GIF often look grainy?
q.why: GIF is lossless but only has 256 colours, so photos look grainy.

q.q: Why should you avoid editing and re-saving the same JPEG many times?
o: It is compressed again each time and loses more quality
It turns into a PSD file
It becomes a larger file each time
q.why: Each re-save of a JPEG compresses it again and loses more quality.

q.q: Which format would you use for a short simple animation?
q.why: GIF is used for simple graphics and short animations.

q.q: Which statement compares lossless and lossy compression correctly?
o: Both keep all quality, but lossy is quicker to open
Lossless gives a smaller file but loses quality; lossy keeps all quality
Lossy gives a smaller file but loses quality; lossless keeps all quality
Both lose quality, but lossless loses less each time
q.why: Lossy is much smaller but quality is lost permanently; lossless is smaller but keeps everything.

q.q: Which package is vector-based and popular with logo designers?
q.why: Illustrator works with vectors, so logos scale easily.

q.q: Where do you find the Photoshop toolbox if it has disappeared?
q.why: Window > Tools brings the toolbox back.

q.q: What does the options bar at the top of Photoshop show?
o: Settings for the currently selected tool
The list of files you have saved
The colours in the Swatches panel
q.why: The options bar changes to match the tool you choose.

q.q: Which two packages are free?
q.why: GIMP and Pixlr are free to use.

q.q: What is a graphics package?
o: A device you draw on with a stylus
A collection of clipart sold on a CD
Software for creating and editing images
A file that stores an image with layers
q.why: A graphics package is software for creating and manipulating images.

q.q: Which graphics package is best suited to beginners?
q.why: Paint suits beginners (novice users) for simple drawing.

q.q: Why does the school use Photoshop rather than Illustrator for editing real photos?
o: Photoshop only works with vector images
Photos are bitmaps and Photoshop is a bitmap package
Photoshop is free for everyone to use
q.why: We want to edit real photographs, which are bitmaps, so we use Photoshop.

q.q: Why is Pixlr a good choice for working on images at home?
o: It comes with the school C2k login
It is a vector package like Illustrator
It is free and runs in a web browser
It is the only package that opens PSD files
q.why: Pixlr is free and runs in a web browser.

q.q: In Photoshop, where is the Layers panel usually found?
o: In the middle of the screen
q.why: The toolbox is on the left, the options bar on top, Colour/Swatches top right and Layers bottom right.

q.q: Which tool selects all neighbouring pixels of a similar colour with one click?
q.why: The Magic Wand selects by colour; tolerance controls how similar.

q.q: What must you do before painting with the Clone Stamp?
o: Hold Alt and click a source area
Press Ctrl + T to transform the layer
q.why: Alt + click picks the area to copy from.

q.q: You want to add a shadow under a cartoon character by darkening part of the image. Which tool should you use?
q.why: Burn darkens; Dodge lightens; Sponge changes colour strength.

q.q: What does the History Brush do?
o: Restores part of the image to an earlier state
Deletes the list of earlier changes
Copies one area of the image over another
Paints over the image in a new colour
q.why: It is like an undo for just the area you paint over.

q.q: What does changing the Magic Wand's tolerance do?
o: Changes the size of the brush
Selects a bigger or smaller range of shades
Changes how dark the selected area becomes
Makes the selection a rectangle or oval
q.why: Tolerance in the options bar selects a bigger or smaller range of shades.

q.q: Which tool picks up a colour from any part of the image so you can use it?
q.why: The Eyedropper samples the colour from the image.

q.q: Which tool 'sticks' to the edge of a shape that contrasts with its background?
q.why: The Magnetic Lasso sticks to the edge of a contrasting shape.

q.q: How do you see the hidden tools under a toolbox button with a small triangle?
o: Hold down the left mouse button on it
q.why: Hold down the left mouse button on a tool with a small triangle to see the others.

q.q: Which keys make the brush smaller or bigger?
q.why: Press [ and ] to make the brush smaller or bigger.

q.q: The Eraser seems to do nothing to your image. What is the most likely reason?
o: The tolerance is set too high
The wrong layer is selected in the Layers panel
The image is saved as a PSD
q.why: The Eraser rubs out part of the selected layer, so check the right layer is selected.

q.q: You have pasted an image that is far too big for your poster. What should you do?
o: Use the Crop tool on the Background layer
Use the Eraser to rub out the edges
Save it as a JPEG to make it smaller
Select its layer and use Free Transform (Ctrl + T)
q.why: Edit > Transform > Free Transform (Ctrl + T) resizes the selected layer.

q.q: Homer has a plain white background you want to delete. Which tool is quickest to select all of it?
q.why: The Magic Wand selects all the touching white pixels in one click, which can then be deleted.

q.q: Why save as .psd before editing?
o: It keeps a working copy with layers that you can keep editing
It is the only file format that Photoshop is able to open
It turns the image into a vector so it never goes pixelated
It compresses the image more than any other format can
q.why: PSD keeps layers and edits.

q.q: What does keeping the 'aspect ratio' mean when resizing?
o: The colours stay exactly the same
The layer stays locked in place
Width and height stay in proportion so it does not stretch
The file size stays the same
q.why: Aspect ratio is the proportion of width to height.

q.q: You want to share your finished Homer image with someone who doesn't have Photoshop and keep its transparent background. What should you do?
o: File > Save As… and choose PNG
q.why: Save As PNG creates an image anyone can open that keeps the transparent background.

q.q: How can you make text stand out with an outline or drop shadow?
o: Press Ctrl + T and drag a corner
Use the History Brush on the text
Right-click the text layer and choose Blending Options
Use the Magic Wand on the text
q.why: In the Layers panel right-click the text layer > Blending Options and add effects such as Stroke or Drop Shadow.

q.q: How can you make a flat 2D shape look 3D?
o: Fill it with the Paint Bucket, then use Burn for shadows and Dodge for shine
Fill it with the Paint Bucket, then use Dodge for shadows and Burn for shine
Use the Clone Stamp to copy it, then press Ctrl + T
Use the Magic Wand, then add a Drop Shadow to the background
q.why: Burn adds shadows (darkens) and Dodge adds shine (lightens).

q.q: When resizing with Free Transform in older Photoshop versions, which key keeps the aspect ratio?
q.why: Holding Shift keeps the aspect ratio (in newer versions it's the default and Shift turns it off).

q.q: What should you do first, before any editing, after opening HOMER.png in Photoshop?
q.why: Before doing anything else, File > Save As a .psd file.

q.q: Why are layers useful?
o: Each element can be moved and edited without affecting the others
They turn bitmap images into vectors so they can be resized
They let the image be printed faster and at a higher DPI
They make the saved file much smaller than a single image
q.why: Layers keep each element independent.

q.q: Which of these is true about the Background layer?
o: It is deleted when you save as .psd
It can be moved to the top of the list
It cannot be moved above other layers or be transparent
q.why: It is locked at the bottom and cannot hold transparency.

q.q: What is the shortcut to paste in Photoshop?
q.why: Ctrl + V pastes; Ctrl + P prints.

q.q: In the Layers panel, which layer appears in front?
o: The one at the top of the list
The one at the bottom of the list
q.why: Higher layers cover the ones below.

q.q: How do you hide a layer in the Layers panel?
o: Click the eye icon next to it
q.why: Click the eye icon to hide or show a layer; double-clicking the name renames it.

q.q: How do you make the Background layer act like a normal layer that can be transparent?
o: Double-click it and press OK so it becomes Layer 0
Save the image as a JPEG
Drag it to the top of the Layers panel
Click the eye icon next to it
q.why: Double-click the Background layer and press OK; it becomes Layer 0.

q.q: Which sequence of shortcuts copies an image and pastes it onto a new layer in another image?
o: Ctrl + A, Ctrl + C, Ctrl + P
Ctrl + A, Ctrl + C, Ctrl + V
Ctrl + T, Ctrl + C, Ctrl + V
Ctrl + C, Ctrl + A, Ctrl + P
q.why: Select all, copy, then paste with Ctrl + V; Ctrl + P is Print.

q.q: What is 'Two Stars and a Wish'?
o: A two-layer Photoshop image with a star-shaped logo on top
Two tools you used well and one tool you want to learn next
A score of two marks out of three for the Pixlr poster task
Two things you liked about a partner's work and one improvement
q.why: Peer assessment: two things you really liked and one improvement they could make.

q.q: You try to move the dragon with the Move tool but the crest moves instead. What is wrong?
o: The crest's layer is selected instead of the dragon's
The image is saved as a PNG
The Magic Wand tolerance is too low
q.why: Tools only affect the selected layer, so select the dragon layer first.
